--- title: "Introduction" guide-section: "Getting Started" bread-crumbs: false --- tinytab is a small library for formatting values and rendering small tables, as text or as HTML. It has no dependencies beyond Python itself. It exists as an example: a small but complete package that shows how to structure, test, and document a Python library. It isn't published on PyPI. ## Installation Install tinytab from its GitHub repository: ```{.bash filename="Terminal"} pip install git+https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package.git ``` ## A first look tinytab does three things. It formats single values as strings: ::: {#4ad8f16f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from tinytab import fmt_currency fmt_currency(1234.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` '$1,234.50' ``` ::: ::: It builds tables, with a formatter attached to any column: ::: {#763cf9c9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from tinytab import Table menu = Table( { "item": ["coffee", "bagel", "croissant"], "price": [3.5, 2.25, 4.0], } ) menu.fmt("price", fmt_currency) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
itemprice
coffee$3.50
bagel$2.25
croissant$4.00
``` ::: ::: And it summarizes sets of numbers: ::: {#0be867e7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from tinytab import summarize summarize([3.5, 2.25, 4.0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` SummaryResult(n=3, mean=3.25, sd=0.9014, min=2.25, max=4) ``` ::: ::: The rest of this guide takes each of these in turn: - [Formatting Values](formatting-values.qmd): numbers, percentages, and currencies - [Tables](tables.qmd): building, formatting, rendering, and saving tables - [Summary Statistics](summary-statistics.qmd): `summarize()` and its result object
